---
title: "Where must the missing 340 g sit to balance inside the CG band?"
subtitle: "The reconstruction predicts 1021 g against 1361 g published, so 340 g of glue, doublers and finish is unmodelled, and where it sits decides whether the published CG band is reachable."
---




::: {.hero}
[721 mm]{.hero-value}
[nominal longitudinal station from nose for unmodelled mass to balance at target CG]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** The [initial reconstruction](2026-10-07-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-f-16-viper-within-tolerance.qmd) revealed a [340 g]{.key} shortfall between predicted airframe mass ([1021 g]{.key}) and published dry mass ([1361 g]{.key}). To balance the assembled airframe inside the published center-of-gravity band ([25\.4--38\.0 mm]{.key} aft of the wing leading edge break), the centroid of this unmodelled mass must sit between [695\.7 mm]{.key} and [746\.1 mm]{.key} from the nose (@fig-missing-mass-balance). Measured relative to the break, this allowable window spans [50\.4 mm]{.key} (from [\-4\.3 mm]{.key} to [46\.1 mm]{.key}). The nominal balance point lands at [720\.9 mm]{.key} ([20\.9 mm]{.key} aft of the break).

Crucially, this allowable band spans the structural core: the wing root joiner, internal intake ducting, electronics bay, and canopy junction ($x \approx$ [700--730 mm]{.key}). Hot glue, plywood reinforcements, and paper finish naturally concentrate in this center-fuselage region. If the unmodelled mass simply shares the Maker Foam cut centroid ([730 mm]{.key}), the finished airframe balances at [34\.0 mm]{.key} aft of the leading edge—comfortably within the published envelope without requiring corrective ballast.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What the code does

Evaluates airframe balance by solving moment equilibrium for the unmodelled 340 g mass against published dry mass and center-of-gravity specifications obtained via check_reconstruction.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The method, as called

```python
def check_reconstruction(airplane, mass_props, cg_aft_le):
    """
    Evaluate reconstructed aircraft dimensions against published specifications.

    Returns dict of target dicts with actual values, tolerances, and error ratios.
    """
    targets = {
        "Wingspan": {
            "target": 0.914,
            "actual": float(airplane.wings[0].span(include_centerline_distance=True)),
            "tol": 0.005,
            "unit": "m",
        },
        "Length": {
            "target": 1.295,
            "actual": float(airplane.fuselages[0].length()),
            "tol": 0.010,
            "unit": "m",
        },
        "Dry mass": {
            "target": 1.361,
            "actual": float(mass_props.mass),
            "tol": 0.050,
            "unit": "kg",
        },
        "CG aft LE": {
            "target": 0.0317,
            "actual": float(cg_aft_le),
            "tol": 0.0063,
            "unit": "m",
        },
    }
    for k, v in targets.items():
        v["abs_err"] = abs(v["actual"] - v["target"])
        v["rel_err"] = v["abs_err"] / v["target"]
        v["tol_frac"] = v["abs_err"] / v["tol"]
    return targets
```
